title: The new helical dichroism driven by vortex beam: Revolutionary breakthroughs in chiral optics
abstract: Chirality plays a fundamental role in chemistry, biology, and materials science, influencing molecular recognition, drug activity, and optical functionality. Traditional chiral analysis methods, such as circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy, have become indispensable, but they are limited by their reliance on a single absorption signal, low sensitivity to weakly chiral systems, and are unable to distinguish materials with complex spatial or multicentric chirality. Vortex beams, carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) with a helical phase structure, introduce an additional spatial degree of freedom that enables helical dichroism (HD) spectroscopy. By tuning the topological charge (TC), HD can achieve multi-dimensional coupled detection of light intensity, phase, polarization and spatial topology, breaking through the one-dimensional limitation of CD. In this work, we review the physical foundation and experimental progress of HD from three perspectives: (1) the interaction mechanism between vortex beams and chiral matter; (2) transmission distortion analysis as a new detection dimension; and (3) AI-driven decoding for multidimensional signal extraction. Together, these advances demonstrate HD’s superior capability in resolving weak, complex, and dynamic chiral structures. Looking forward, integrating HD with metasurface control, intelligent signal processing, and on-chip detection is expected to establish a new generation of high-dimensional, adaptive chiral spectroscopy, paving the way for AI-assisted, chip-scale platforms capable of precise and real-time enantioselective analysis.

title: Design and synthesis of Ti3C2 and Ti3C2Tx MXenes for sensing, energy, and electromagnetic interference shielding: Advancing multifunctional applications with machine learning-assisted material design
abstract: The development and creation of MXenes, a novel class of two-dimensional (2D) early transition metal carbides and carbonitrides, have demonstrated numerous appealing properties and hold significant potential for energy storage and various other applications. More specifically, Ti 3 C 2 and Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes (T x stands for surface terminating species, including O, OH, and F) have garnered widespread attention due to their excellent electrical conductivity, remarkable flexibility, and customisable surface chemistry, making them exceptionally suitable in sensing applications, including strain/stress sensors, gas sensors, and biosensors. Several fabrication processes, including thin film deposition, hydrogel synthesis, and composite integration, have been explored to enhance sensor performance and stability. Specifically, their higher surface area and metallic conductivity make them highly promising candidates for electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, as well as energy storage and conversion applications. Next-level approaches, such as surface modification, composite design, and device engineering, are being sought to overcome the challenges related to material stability and its scalability. Through a comprehensive analysis of recent advancements and prospects, this review aims to provide worthy perceptions into the potential of Ti 3 C 2 and Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes for the development of innovative solutions in spanning sensing, energy, and intelligent robotics fields, with implications for a wide range of industries and scientific research endeavours.

title: Beyond manual processing: Robotic-arm automation coupled with machine learning for precision control and correlation insights in perovskite solar cells
abstract: Spin coating, widely used in perovskite solar cell research, is inherently limited by manual processing, leading to uncontrollable process parameters. A major challenge lies in the anti-solvent dripping process, where precise control of dripping speed by manual methods is impractical. Consequently, quantitative analysis of thin films and device performance based on dripping speed has remained challenging, despite its significant impact on film quality. To address this limitation, we developed a fully customized robotic arm-based system that precisely mimics human motion while enabling quantitative control of previously unmanageable parameters. This automated system systematically explores the effects of various process variables, including anti-solvent chemical properties, through machine learning-driven data analysis.

title: Stabilizing DNA origami nanostructures for clinical translation through chemical and computational engineering
abstract: However, despite their tremendous therapeutic potential for sensing and delivery, DNA origamis cannot be used for the development of therapeutic agents due to three interrelated physiological barriers: degradation through nucleases, structural collapse under low ionic strength conditions, and instability in biological fluid temperatures. The recent developments in the field include chemical modification, cross-linking, and computational designs, which individually increase stability several times. Yet, even using phosphorothioate backbone, ultraviolet (UV) cross-linking, and machine learning techniques separately allows achieving only an order of magnitude improvement. In the current paper, we comprehensively analyzed the combination effect on the stability provided by protective coating, covalent modification, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted sequence optimization for generating DNA origami with an increase of stability by thousands of times and presented a dedicated mathematical model proving a synergic effect in applying the strategies orthogonal to each other. Moreover, we considered the critical problem of scaling DNA origamis up from laboratory grams of production to industrial kilos, analyzing costs of staples' synthesis, GMP purification process, and complex regulatory requirements from Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency (EMA), Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) regarding medical product classification. Finally, we discussed the key importance of large datasets generation in DNA origami research for successful use of machine learning.
